summary: Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Gerd J. R. Mevissen held posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter in 2026.

Gereon Kopf studied at Temple University (~1991–1996) and under Yasuo Yuasa. He researched at J. F. Oberlin University (1993–1994) and Nanzan University (2002–2004), and taught at Luther College (~1997) and the University of Hong Kong.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Gergely Hidas studied at Eötvös Loránd University, Balliol College, and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Csaba Töttössy, and Ferenc Ruzsa. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Meiser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Albertus-Magnus-Gymnasium Regensburg, the University of Regensburg (~1971–1975), the University of Munich (~1975–1979), the University of Freiburg (~1979–1983), and the universities of Belgrade and Sarajevo.

A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Gerhard Oberhammer studied at the University of Innsbruck (~1948–1954) and the Sorbonne (~1957–1958) under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (1964–1997).
Gerhard Wolf studied at Heidelberg University (~1975–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).
Specializing in philosophy, Gernot Böhme studied at the University of Hamburg (~1960–1965) and held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt (~1977–2002).

Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Tübingen (~1961–1963), the University of Bonn (~1967–1970), and under Annemarie Schimmel (~1962–1967). He held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1984–2004).

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld specialized in Indology. He studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1974) under Jan Gonda (~1954–1974) and served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen (1978–1986).

Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Gert Klingenschmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1961–1976), where he was an assistant (~1969–1976), before holding a chair at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Gendun Lodro studied at Drepung Monastery, Drepung Gomang Dratsang, and under Khensur Ngawang Legden. He held posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).

Geshe Jampa Tegchok, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1992) and as resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam, who worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, held posts attested at Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and Sera Monastery in 1992.

Geshe Lhakdor studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served at Tibet House (1986–1989), the University of British Columbia (2002), and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (2005).

Geshe Lhundup Sopa studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey under Geshe Lhundrup Tabkhe, Geshe Ngawang Rigsal, Geshe Ngawang Gendun, and Lhundrub Tsöndrü. He worked at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 and founded Deer Park Buddhist Center in 1976.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Lobsang Tharchin studied at Sera Monastery until 1953, earning the Lharampa Geshe degree, and at Gyume Tantric College.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Geshe Losang Chödar held posts attested in 2010 at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Geshe Ngawang Nyima held posts at Drepung Monastery, Drepung Gomang Dratsang, Leiden University, and served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Geshe Ngawang Samten studied at CIHTS and Ganden Shartse Monastery under multiple traditional teachers. He served as CIHTS Chief Editor (~1988–2021) and held posts at the University of Tasmania (~1994), Hampshire and Amherst Colleges (~1997–1998), and Smith College (2004).
Geshe Palden Dragpa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, where he is attested as librarian between 1987 and 1992, and further attested in 2004.
